messages:
jordan: Ran a 40m nsys sampling trace on the 32k-seqlen repro. Seeing repeated HBM bandwidth spikes that line up with KV cache eviction waves. Attaching short snippet from the timeline and a quick summary below.

perf-bot: nsys report available: https://perf.redwood.dev/trace/1825001234 (sampling) :spiral_calendar:

jordan: Quick numbers from the run: peak HBM read ~ 720 GB/s, sustained bursts ~ 420-480 GB/s for 100-300ms every ~2s. GPU active % high but kernels are very short (~0.2-2ms) with lots of memcpy syncs. KV read latency distribution shows bimodal tail.

sasha: Can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? curious if it's the attention kernel switching or something in kv page handling.

jordan: Paste of the timeline (trimmed):

```
TIME(ms)  KERNEL                          GPU    DUR(ms)  HBMRead(GB)
0         fused_attn_forward_v1           0      1.8       12
1.9       fused_attn_forward_v2           0      0.6       40
2.6       kv_page_read_async              0      0.12      80
2.72      cudaMemcpyAsync                0      0.05      10
2.78      fused_attn_forward_v2           0      0.7       50
... (repeats pattern)
```

Observation: the heavy HBM reads map to the async KV page reads which trigger short but intense bursts. The switching between attn_v1/v2 seems to change memory access patterns and causes more page churn.

lee: Hmm that looks like microbatching + kernel selection oscillation. If the batching heuristic picks different kernels depending on seq-padding distribution, we can end up with tiny kernel invocations that repeatedly touch different KV pages. That would thrash HBM.

natalie: What's the batching config you used for this trace? especially microbatch cap, prefetch depth, and cache page size.

jordan: Config used (defaults except where noted):
```
batch.max_microbatch = 16
batch.prefetch_pages = 8
kv.cache_page_size = 64KB
evict.threshold = 0.9
kernel.selection.mode = auto
```

I suspect kv.cache_page_size being small + prefetch depth leads to more parallel page reads. Also kernel.selection.mode=auto triggers v1/v2 flip based on observed seq length, causing inconsistent memory strides.

sasha: Two quick mitigations to try: 1) increase kv.cache_page_size to 256KB to reduce number of page reads, 2) add a sticky kernel choice for short windows so selection doesn't flip within a request batch.

lee: Also try capping microbatch to 8 for large seq runs; the throughput drop is modest but it can greatly reduce concurrent page reads. We should also check if our kv async read coalescing is actually coalescing - timeline suggests many tiny async reads.

jordan: I ran a follow-up 10m sampling with kv.cache_page_size=256KB and microbatch cap=8. Result: peak HBM read down to ~520 GB/s, bursts shorter and less frequent, latency p95 improved by ~18% for large sequences.

perf-bot: New nsys report: https://perf.redwood.dev/trace/1825001299 (config: page=256k, micro=8)

natalie: Great. Did that change affect small/medium seq workloads? Need to verify we didn't regress 2k-4k latency.

jordan: Quick perf smoke: 2k seq p95 unchanged (+1%), throughput within noise. So win for large seqs without regress.

lee: Long-term fix ideas: - add hysteresis to kernel selection so we don't flip on small distribution changes - implement an async coalescer that aggregates KV page read requests across concurrent microbatches - consider adaptive page sizing per-model or per-request class

sasha: Agree. Also add a perf test in CI that runs a synthetic 32k-seqlen workload and checks HBM read tail. Current testbench only checks latency, not HBM pattern.

jordan: I'll open a short PR: 1) default kv.cache_page_size bumped to 256KB for large_seq profiles, 2) add kernel selection sticky flag, 3) add a perf regression job (nsys sampling) for 32k. Will link PR here when ready.

deploy-bot: Reminder: tests on CI are queued (approx 45m).

sasha: One more ask — can you also attach the raw nsys sample export (top20 kernels by HBMRead)? that will help us prioritize kernel fusion opportunities.

jordan: Uploaded top kernels CSV to the trace page and added a table to the issue. Top 3 HBM consumers: kv_page_read_async, fused_attn_forward_v2, aten::index_select. KV read is the biggest contributor.

lee: If index_select is pulling lots of small gathers, we should evaluate replacing it with a fused gather kernel that aligns better with page granularity. Good to know.

jordan: Notes for the issue: reproduction script, nsys commands used, timeline screenshots, config diff, and preliminary perf runs are in the PR. Will run a longer 2h trace overnight to be certain.

natalie: Thanks — please include the CI perf job config so we can run it from staging infra as well.

jordan: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
